summary: Spanish splits the domain among ser, estar, existential haber (hay), and other constructions; permanent/temporary is not an adequate decision rule.

semantic_map.SEM.CHARACTERISTIC_PROPERTY: ser for characteristic/classificatory predication; adjective-specific contrasts require separate rules
semantic_map.SEM.CURRENT_STATE: estar for many states/conditions; lexical adjective and discourse context matter
semantic_map.SEM.RESULTANT_STATE: estar + adjective/participle for many resultant states
semantic_map.SEM.ENTITY_LOCATION: estar for location of known entities
semantic_map.SEM.EXISTENCE_PRESENCE: impersonal haber, present hay, for existence/presentation
semantic_map.SEM.ABSENCE_NONEXISTENCE: no hay / impersonal haber under negation
semantic_map.SEM.ORIGIN_AFFILIATION: ser de / ser + nationality or affiliation
semantic_map.SEM.POSSESSION_AS_EXISTENCE: not default; dedicated tener is ordinary possession
